Description: A documentary-style program narrated by Bill Buck, with contributions from Dr. Rashad Khalifa, presenting the Quran's mathematical code as what it calls the ultimate miracle. The first half argues that modern people cannot be convinced by the localized miracles of earlier ages and need something perpetual, physical and verifiable, then surveys passages the program reads as anticipating modern science: embryology confirmed by Dr. Moore of the University of Toronto, the three veils of darkness, the Big Bang, the preserved body of Pharaoh, the moon as a reflector rather than a source of light, an egg-shaped Earth, the atmosphere as a protective ceiling, water as a requisite of every living thing, honey from the bee's belly, milk formed between urine and blood, plants created in pairs, moving mountains, mountains as stakes, and fingerprints, citing Maurice Bucaille's assessment that a fourteen-hundred-year-old text could not contain such ideas. The second half explains the code itself, using "Jack and Jill went up the hill" to show how hard it is to alter a sentence's letter counts while keeping its meaning, then reports the counts of the Quranic initials, the nineteen letters and four words of the opening statement with their totals of 19, 2698, 57 and 114, and the 6346 verses across 114 chapters. It closes with 19 as a signature the program finds in the 209 bones of the body and the 266 days of gestation, explains that 19 is the numerical value of the Arabic word for one, and argues that the code authenticates the earlier miracles of Moses and Jesus.
